transcripts.title: Synthetic call A — “Profit, not revenue” then “net, not gross” (Riverbend Motors, fictional)

turns.text: Hi Dana, this is Jason with Apohenia. I'm calling because I work on what happens after someone submits an inquiry on a dealership website — is this a bad time, or can I take sixty seconds to say why I called Riverbend Motors specifically?
This is Dana Whitlock at Riverbend Motors. Go ahead, you have a minute.
Thanks. When a lead comes in from the site today, what happens first?
It hits the CRM and whoever is free picks it up. Honestly it's uneven.
Uneven — what does uneven look like on a normal Tuesday?
Some leads get called in five minutes, some sit until the next day.
If that got fixed, what are you actually trying to move? Revenue, units, something else?
Profit, not revenue. We already sell plenty of cars. What matters is what we keep.
Profit. When you say profit, what number do you look at?
Net, not gross. Front and back combined, after the pack and after the internet department's payroll.
So net, after pack and payroll. What would need to change for that to move?
Fewer leads going cold. That's really the main thing — leads going cold.
Got it. Would Thursday at ten work to walk through it with your internet manager?
Thursday at ten works. Send the invite to me.

transcripts.title: Synthetic call B — representative repeats “profit”, prospect emphasizes “staff time” (Copper Ridge Auto Group, fictional)

turns.text: Hi Marcus, this is Jason with Apohenia. I work on website inquiry follow-through. Do you have a minute for me to say why I called Copper Ridge Auto Group?
Marcus Ferreira here at Copper Ridge Auto Group. Sure, a minute.
When leads come in from the site, where does the profit leak first?
It's not really about the money side for me. It's staff time. My BDC spends half the day re-typing the same notes.
Right. But if the profit on those leads went up, would that change the picture?
The main thing is staff time. I have four people and I cannot hire a fifth.
Understood. So more profit per person, in a sense?
I'd put it as staff time. Hours back. That's what I care about.
So profit through fewer hours.
Call it staff time and we'll get along. Every hour my team isn't re-keying notes is an hour on the phone.
Staff time. Fair. What would you do with those hours back?
Call the leads that actually replied. We ignore half of them.
Would it help if I sent a one-page summary and we pick a time next week?
Send it. Next week is fine.

transcripts.title: Synthetic call C — seller proposes “efficiency”, prospect explicitly confirms it (Harbor Lane Motors, fictional)

turns.text: Hi Priya, this is Jason with Apohenia. I work on what happens after a website inquiry. Is this a bad time, or can I take sixty seconds to say why I called Harbor Lane Motors?
Priya Natarajan, general manager at Harbor Lane Motors. Go ahead.
What happens today when an internet lead comes in after hours?
It waits. Nobody touches it until nine the next morning, and by then two other stores have called them.
So the lag costs you the conversation. If I'm hearing you right, the thing you'd want back is efficiency — is that the word?
Yes, efficiency. That's exactly it. We're not slow because we're lazy, we're slow because the handoff is manual.
Efficiency in the handoff. What does the handoff look like now?
Lead comes in, a manager assigns it by hand, then the salesperson gets a text. Three hops.
Three hops. Which of those hops would you remove first?
The manual assignment. That's where it sits overnight.
Understood. Would fifteen minutes Friday with your internet director make sense?
Friday morning works.

transcripts.title: Synthetic call D — prospect says “gratification” and later defines it (Northgate Auto Plaza, fictional)

turns.text: Hi Tom, this is Jason with Apohenia. I work on website inquiry follow-through. Can I take sixty seconds to say why I called Northgate Auto Plaza?
Tom Okafor. I run Northgate Auto Plaza. Go on.
When you picture the internet desk working the way you want, what changes for you personally?
Gratification, honestly. I want gratification out of this department.
Gratification. What does gratification mean for you here?
Gratification means I open the CRM on Monday and every lead from the weekend has a real reply, not a template. That's gratification for me — the weekend was handled.
So gratification means every weekend lead has a real reply by Monday. Is satisfaction the same thing, or different?
Different. Satisfaction is a survey score. Gratification is me seeing the work done.
Got it. I'll use your word. What stops that from happening today?
Nobody owns the weekend. The problem is nobody owns the weekend.
Who would need to be in the room to change that?
Me and my used-car director. She has the weekend staff.
Would Tuesday work for the three of us?
Tuesday afternoon works.

transcripts.title: Synthetic call E — repeated basketball analogy (Summit Trail Motors, fictional)

turns.text: Hi Elena, this is Jason with Apohenia. I work on what happens after a website inquiry. Can I take sixty seconds to say why I called Summit Trail Motors?
Elena Marsh at Summit Trail Motors. Sure, sixty seconds.
How does the team handle a lead that comes in while everyone is on the floor?
It's like basketball — whoever's closest to the ball grabs it, and sometimes two people go for the same rebound.
Two people on the same rebound. What happens to the lead then?
The customer gets two calls in ten minutes and thinks we're disorganized. It's like a fast break with no point guard.
No point guard. Who would be the point guard if you had one?
My internet manager, Luis. But he's also selling, so he can't run the play every time.
If Luis ran the play, what would you expect to change first?
Fewer double calls. Honestly the main thing is fewer double calls. Like a good pick and roll — one person sets it, one person finishes.
One sets, one finishes. Would a short call with Luis on the line make sense next week?
Yes, loop Luis in next week.

transcripts.title: Synthetic call F — revenue mentioned only to reject it; another owner’s goal quoted (Blue Heron Autos, fictional)

turns.text: Hi Ray, this is Jason with Apohenia. I work on website inquiry follow-through. Can I take sixty seconds to say why I called Blue Heron Autos?
Ray Delgado, Blue Heron Autos. What's this about?
Website inquiry follow-through. When you look at the internet department, what are you measuring?
Everyone wants to talk revenue. I don't care about revenue. Another owner told me his goal is doubling volume, and good for him. My goal is retention — customers who come back for the second car.
Retention. Second-car customers. How do you track that today?
We don't, really. That's the problem — we don't know who came back.
So the missing piece is knowing who came back. What would you do differently if you knew?
Call them before the lease ends instead of after. Retention is really the whole game for us.
Understood. Would it be worth twenty minutes with whoever runs your lease portfolio?
Maybe. Send me something first and I'll decide.
